<STRUCT_0001>
In Situation <REF_0001> we can study the completion functor
Cohomology of Schemes, Equation (<REF_0002>)
<MATH_0001>
If <MATH_0002> is <MATH_0003>-adically complete, then this functor is fully faithful
on suitable subcategories by our earlier work on algebraization of
formal sections, see Section <REF_0003> and
Lemma <REF_0004> for some sample results.
Next, let <MATH_0004> be an object of <MATH_0005>.
Still assuming <MATH_0006> is <MATH_0007>-adically complete, we can ask:
When is <MATH_0008> in the essential image of the completion
functor displayed above?

In Situation <REF_0001> let <MATH_0001>
be an object of <MATH_0002>. Consider the
following conditions:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0003> is in the essential image
of the functor (<REF_0002>),
<STRUCT_0003> <MATH_0004> is the completion of a
coherent <MATH_0005>-module,
<STRUCT_0004> <MATH_0006> is the completion of a coherent
<MATH_0007>-module for <MATH_0008> open,
<STRUCT_0005> <MATH_0009> is the completion of
the restriction to <MATH_0010> of a coherent <MATH_0011>-module,
<STRUCT_0006> <MATH_0012> is the restriction to <MATH_0013> of
the completion of a coherent <MATH_0014>-module,
<STRUCT_0007> there exists an object <MATH_0015> of
<MATH_0016> whose restriction
to <MATH_0017> is <MATH_0018>.
<STRUCT_0008>
Then conditions (1), (2), (3), (4), and (5) are equivalent and imply (6).
If <MATH_0019> is <MATH_0020>-adically complete then condition (6) implies the others.
